hyps.why: Adding a 3x3 conv to a removed final edge restores a major path into the output, gaining more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing 'none' with a conv adds a new learnable path to the output, gaining more than swapping among non-empty ops.
Giving the direct input-to-output edge a conv when it was empty yields a large gain compared with replacing a pool or skip.
Reconnecting node 1 to node 2 with a conv adds depth and capacity that a non-empty edge already partly provides.
Filling an empty edge with a conv gives more benefit than replacing an op that already carries features.
Removing a 3x3 conv from the first edge hurts far more than removing a weak op like avg_pool.
Downgrading a conv to a parameter-free skip on the last edge loses much more accuracy than replacing a weak op.
Swapping a conv for pooling on the direct edge loses learnable capacity, unlike swapping from a weak op.
Deleting a conv edge into the output costs far more accuracy than deleting an edge that was already weak.
With the 0->2 edge missing, node 2 depends on the 0->1->2 route, so a strong conv on edge 0 matters more.
